clue.text: Ways to confuse testers

indicators.note: confusing something muddles its order, so the following word's letters get jumbled

blocks.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone plotting routes designed to bewilder people running trials.
explanation.definitionFit: Roads in a town are thoroughfares, and a way is another general word for a road or route.

clue.text: Eliot embraces composer's passages

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, so the poet's initials wrap around the composer

blocks.note: the poet T. S. Eliot, by his initials
Maurice Ravel, the French composer of Bolero

explanation.surface: The poet Eliot quoting long stretches of a composer's music in his work.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s is read as 'composer is' inside the assembly; Eliot here is reduced to his initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Passages are journeys from place to place, as in a sea passage, which is what travels are.

clue.text: Be an alien consuming elevenses?

indicators.note: consuming means eating, so the alien takes the elevens inside itself

blocks.note: read as eleven-ses, the plural of XI, the Roman numeral for eleven

explanation.surface: An alien tucking into a mid-morning snack.
explanation.walkthrough: Elevenses is a British mid-morning snack, but here it is split as plural elevens, XIs, with the S kept.
explanation.definitionFit: To be is simply to have existence, the most basic verb for being alive or real.

clue.text: Most unbelievable to be wholly involved in trial

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to sit within it, so one word goes inside another

blocks.note: wholly means entirely, all of it

explanation.surface: A courtroom tale: the most far-fetched account of being caught up in a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: A tall story is one hard to believe, so tall means unbelievable here, not high.
explanation.definitionFit: From the idiom tall tale, tall can mean exaggerated or implausible, so the superlative is hardest to credit.

clue.text: Reader of the Sun standing outside church

indicators.note: standing outside puts one word around another, like a guard round a building

blocks.note: CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Someone reading the Sun newspaper while waiting outside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun looks like the tabloid newspaper, but it gives the adjective for the star. A reader is also a British university lecturing rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A reader is a learned person who studies texts closely, and a scholar is an academic devoted to study.

clue.text: Tuck right into finish

indicators.note: putting one thing into another places it inside that word

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: An instruction for making a bed: tuck the right side in to complete it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tuck is a fold sewn or pressed into fabric, and a crease is likewise a fold line.

clue.text: Watching old boy waiting on tables

blocks.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A former pupil seen working as a waiter in a restaurant.
explanation.walkthrough: An old boy is a British term for a former pupil of a school.
explanation.definitionFit: Observing and watching both mean looking at something attentively over time.

clue.text: Fauna and flora finally killed reversing over motorway

indicators.note: finally keeps just the closing letter of the word before it
one word lying over another here wraps around it
reversing means going backwards, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: M is used for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A grim scene of plants and wildlife mown down beside a motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: SLAIN wraps the M to make SLAMIN, which turns round and follows the A.
explanation.definitionFit: Fauna is the collective term for the animal life of a region, as flora is for plants.

clue.text: Devising team, initially for a clever code-breaker

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the next words

blocks.note: Man U, short for Manchester United football club
Alan Turing, the Bletchley Park code-breaker

explanation.surface: A team coming up with a scheme to suit a brilliant codebreaker.
explanation.walkthrough: Man U is the familiar name for Manchester United, an English football club.
explanation.definitionFit: Manufacturing can mean inventing or concocting, as in manufacturing an excuse, so it matches devising.

clue.text: Transport head of the A-team

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: a cricket or football team is an eleven, XI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: The leader of the A-Team's famous van, from the TV action series.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxi is a vehicle for hire that carries people around, a form of transport.

clue.text: Aid helpers to develop direction

indicators.note: developing something changes its form, so these letters are reshaped

blocks.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice on supporting assistants so that they grow in their roles.
explanation.definitionFit: Direction in the sense of guidance and management of people is what leadership provides.

clue.text: Scoot along in a car

explanation.surface: Someone zipping about town in a little car.
explanation.walkthrough: To beetle along is informal British for scurrying quickly; the Volkswagen Beetle is the classic small car.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for moving briskly and the name of a famous rounded Volkswagen model.

clue.text: Tamper with us struggling against the current

indicators.note: something struggling is thrashing about, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Swimmers complaining about interference while battling a strong tide.
explanation.definitionFit: Going upstream means travelling toward a river's source, moving opposite to the flow of water.

clue.text: Required to be moved — in the wrong aisle!

indicators.note: something wrong is out of order, so the letters of the last word are rearranged
in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: moved emotionally, as in sent into raptures

explanation.surface: Someone told to shift because they are standing in the wrong supermarket aisle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Moved' looks like part of the instruction, but it is the emotional sense, sent.
explanation.definitionFit: Something essential is necessary or indispensable, which is what required means.

clue.text: Immunity from the next poem I compose

indicators.note: composing builds something new out of material, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A poet asking to be let off writing the next poem.
explanation.walkthrough: Only 'next poem I' is fodder; 'the' belongs to the surface sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: An exemption is a release from an obligation or rule, the same as immunity from it.

clue.text: "S'pity", slurred under the influence!

indicators.note: slurred speech runs sounds together out of order, so the letters are mixed

blocks.note: the anagram fodder, ignoring the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A drunk person mumbling 'it's a pity' with garbled words.
explanation.definitionFit: Being under the influence is an idiom for being affected by alcohol, which is what tipsy means.

clue.text: Rush around Deep South

indicators.note: turning around means facing the other way, so the two pieces are read backwards together

blocks.note: taken as written; that the full words also run backwards is a coincidence, as only the abbreviation of the second is used
S is the abbreviation for South

explanation.surface: Hurrying around the American Deep South.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deep South' looks like a single place name, the southern US states, but it is the word plus an abbreviation, turned round together.
explanation.definitionFit: To speed is to go fast or hurry, so it works as a verb for rush.

clue.text: Argue for examination

explanation.surface: Someone making the case in favour of holding an exam.
explanation.definitionFit: To protest can mean to argue or assert strongly, as in protesting one's innocence.

clue.text: Is it wrong best leaders are deposed as the most powerful?

indicators.note: deposing leaders removes the ones at the front, so each word loses its opening letter

blocks.note: taken as written before losing its head
taken as written before losing its head
taken as written before losing its head
taken as written before losing its head

explanation.surface: A political question: is it wrong that the top people get overthrown?
explanation.walkthrough: Leaders looks like it means first letters to keep, but deposed means they are removed from all four words.
explanation.definitionFit: The strongest is the one with greatest strength or might, a direct synonym for most powerful.

clue.text: Subdue work by journalists

blocks.note: OP, short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: A reporter's article aimed at silencing someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppress is to keep people down by harsh control, which is a way to subdue them.

clue.text: Space for keeping silver in shop

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

blocks.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A jeweller's shop needing room to keep its silverware.
explanation.definitionFit: Storage is room set aside for holding goods, so it is space for keeping things.

clue.text: Figure standing right away

indicators.note: sending something away removes it from the word

blocks.note: standing in the sense of status or reputation
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A figure standing upright, someone straightening up immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right away' reads as immediately, but it means drop the R; standing is reputation, not being upright.
explanation.definitionFit: A statue is a sculpted figure of a person or animal, so figure fits as its synonym.

clue.text: Conservative leader, politician needing external cover from PC

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
needing a cover means the politician sits inside another word

explanation.surface: A Tory leader and an MP needing protection from a police constable.
explanation.walkthrough: PC looks like a police constable, the British rank, but it is the computer.
explanation.definitionFit: PC stands for personal computer, the common desktop or laptop machine.

clue.text: Spoil gutted fish in Paris

indicators.note: gutting a fish takes out its insides, so a middle letter is removed

explanation.surface: A cook in Paris ruining a fish by gutting it.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one of the doubled S letters in the middle is taken out.
explanation.definitionFit: To poison something can mean to corrupt or ruin it, as in poisoning a friendship, so it means spoil.

clue.text: I help Northern Ireland rise

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means reading the letters upward, from bottom to top

explanation.surface: Someone vowing to help Northern Ireland prosper.
explanation.walkthrough: I looks like the speaker, but it is the definition: India is the code word for I in the NATO phonetic alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: In the radio spelling alphabet each letter has a code word, and the one for letter I is India.

clue.text: Stand in as secret is out

indicators.note: out can mean disordered or wrong, so the letters before it are rearranged

blocks.note: the anagram fodder, taken as written

explanation.surface: An understudy stepping in now that a secret has leaked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stand in' looks like one phrase for an understudy, but Stand alone is the definition and 'in' starts the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a stand against something is offering opposition, which is what resistance means.

clue.text: Unaware of having somewhat made a fuss

indicators.note: somewhat means partly, so only part of the following words is used

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: Someone oblivious to having kicked up a fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Being deaf to something, such as pleas, means refusing to notice it, so the word suggests unaware.

clue.text: Shocked as naughty nun is hugged by Saint Edward

indicators.note: something naughty misbehaves, so these letters are put out of order
being hugged means held inside someone's arms, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A scandal: a misbehaving nun embraced by a saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Stunned describes someone dazed with astonishment, which matches being shocked.

clue.text: Ran off to get key copied

blocks.note: the Escape key on a computer keyboard

explanation.surface: Someone fleeing to have a door key duplicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Key copied' suggests a locksmith, but the key is on a keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who escaped got away from captivity, which is to run off.
